The genuinely still-open piece is a NEW, separately bid ~325 km Jammu-Srinagar tender (PNGRB approved bidding Dec-2023, invited bids Jan-2024, deadline May-2024, no awardee found in any source through Aug-2026) that has no GEM row at all -- flag as a Discovery candidate if Update wants to keep tracking the live remainder rather than retiring P0908 outright.
concerns.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/DUPLICATE finding, not a hallucination -- this corridor is very real and extensively reported since 2011, but P0908 as currently modeled (single 725 km Bhatinda->Srinagar pipeline, Owner1=Gujarat State Petronet/GIGL consortium, Status=proposed) describes an authorization that PNGRB formally voided years ago, while the physical corridor has since been re-let as THREE separate authorizations, two of which GEM already tracks as their own rows. Sequence, corroborated by three independent outlets: (1) boldnewsonline.com, 2023-02-22: 'The Bhatinda-Jammu-Srinagar pipeline was previously authorized to the GSPL-led consortium, which later became GSPL India Gasnet Limited (GIGL). However, GIGL/GSPL failed to complete the pipeline up to Srinagar, prompting PNGRB to foreclose the pipeline at Gurdaspur and launch a new proposal for the Gurdaspur-Jammu gas pipeline.' (2) psuwatch.com, 2023-06-22, and (3) business-standard.com, 2023-06-22 (same day, GAIL's award announcement): both state 'Originally, the Bhatinda-Jammu-Srinagar natural gas pipeline was awarded to Gujarat State Petronet Ltd (GSPL)-led consortium... GIGL failed to lay the pipeline within the stipulated time, following which PNGRB cancelled the authorisation' and PNGRB then 'disqualified GIGL and its lead partner GSPL from submitting bid for the proposed [Gurdaspur-Jammu] pipeline,' which GAIL then won (175 km, financial bids evaluated 2023-06-21). So the foreclosure boundary is exactly Gurdaspur: GIGL's Bhatinda-Gurdaspur grant (07.07.2011) survived intact -- confirmed still active, same entity/date, in the repo's own PNGRB MIS register crosswalk (batches/india-gas/staging/register-crosswalk/pngrb_ngpl_mis.json, 'partially_commissioned' section, sno 2, entity=GIGL, authorised 261 km, 101 km operating) -- and that is P3913 (GEM: Bhatinda-Gurdaspur, 290 km, GIGL, construction). The foreclosed Gurdaspur-onward stretch was re-bid and won by GAIL in 2023; that is P5413 (GEM: Gurdaspur-Jammu, 175 km, construction), and the same register lists it under_construction, entity=GAIL, authorised 160 km, target Jul-26 -- work confirmed physically underway by dailyexcelsior.com 2024-12-05/2026 coverage (37 km Kathua + 38 km Samba + remainder to Jammu Ring Road). PNGRB then separately opened a NEW tender for the final Jammu-Srinagar leg: PNGRB press release 2023-12-27 approved bidding; kashmirobserver.net 2024-01-19 and swarajyamag.com report a 325 km line 'commencing from the endpoint of the Gurdaspur-Jammu pipeline being implemented by GAIL... and extend[ing] up to Srinagar,' minimum capacity 2 MMSCMD, bids due 2024-05-13. No award, construction start, or cancellation for THIS tender turned up in any search through 2025-2026 -- it may itself be genuinely stalled (>2y with no news since the May-2024 bid deadline), but that is a separate, not-yet-GEM-tracked entity, not evidence about P0908 as recorded. Net: P0908's Owner (GIGL, matching P5411's exact 52/26/11/11 GSPL/IOCL/BPCL/HPCL split) is the wrong entity for anything past Gurdaspur -- GIGL was expressly disqualified from that ground -- and its 725 km length silently re-states mileage GEM already counts, correctly, under P3913 and P5413. Secondary SPEC caveat (not the primary concern, noted for completeness): P0908's Capacity=15.48 bcm/y does not reconcile with any register figure for this corridor (Mehsana-Bhatinda 83.1 MMSCMD, Bhatinda-Gurdaspur 42.4 MMSCMD, Gurdaspur-Jammu 3.1 MMSCMD, new Jammu-Srinagar minimum 2 MMSCMD) nor with the one open-web figure found ('designed to transport approximately 31 MMSCMD initially from Bathinda to Jammu' -- itself a single, non-independently-verified mention); left untouched rather than guessed at.

concerns.researcher_notes: P6562's own Wiki field points at https://www.gem.wiki/Kanai_Chhata-Shrirampur_Gas_Pipeline -- the IDENTICAL wiki URL recorded for a wholly separate GEM ProjectID, P2214 ('Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur Gas Pipeline'), per data/GGIT_gas_snapshot_20260810.csv. Read for leads only (never cited): that wiki page's own prose states the pipeline was 'Originally the Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur Gas Pipeline, later re-named as Kanai Chhata-Panitar Gas Pipeline' and that a '2022: Route amendment approved, changing terminus from Shrirampur, Maharashtra to Panitar, West Bengal' -- i.e. gem.wiki itself documents these as ONE project's two successive identities, not two pipelines. Independent, non-GEM corroboration of the SAME lineage found via open web search (a secondary infrastructure-database description of the original PNGRB authorisation): the July 2019 authorisation was for 242 km 'from Kanai Chhata in East Medinipur, to Shrirampur in Nadia, West Bengal' at capacity 19.2 MMSCMD (unchanged since); PNGRB approved a route amendment in 2022 moving the terminus to Panitar and the length to 317 km. Every fact GEM's two rows disagree on lines up with 'same project, two dates': ProposalYear 2019 on both, Capacity 19.2 MMSCMD on both (unchanged across the amendment), only Length (250 vs 317 km) and EndLocation/EndState (Shrirampur/Maharashtra vs Panitar/West Bengal) differ -- exactly what a route amendment would change. Since P2214 already reads 'cancelled', there is no live double-count in country under-construction totals, so I am not flagging this as a data-quality emergency -- but leaving both rows unlinked risks a future researcher treating P2214 as a genuinely separate, previously-real 250 km Maharashtra-bound line that fell through, when the evidence says it is this same 317 km West Bengal project before its 2022 reroute.

concerns.researcher_notes: Started from the sheet's own wiki citations, all pngrb.gov.in. The PNGRB authorization number cited (PNGRB/Auth/2-NGPL/BID/KSPL/(8)/2019) is the SAME number printed on a 01-Aug-2022 PNGRB letter I downloaded and read directly (image-only scan, no text layer, so I rendered it to PNG and read it visually since url_verifier's substring check cannot parse scanned PDFs): 'Amendment in letter of Grant of Authorization for Kanai Chhata - Shrirampur Natural Gas pipeline due to shifting of termination point from Shrirampur to Panitar', addressed to HPPL director Abhirup Bhattacharya, approving the shift 'as per sub-regulation (3) of Regulation 13' and revising the authorized trunk length from 242 km to 266 km. I then pulled two PNGRB national-register PDFs at different dates and grepped the extracted text (pdftotext -layout): the 25-Jun-2021 register (pre-amendment) lists row 5.11.NGPL as 'Kanai Chhata - Shrirampur', sponsor HPPL, auth date 08.07.2019, 317 km, 19.20 (capacity), target 'July, 2022', West Bengal; the 26-Jun-2024 register (post-amendment) lists the SAME row number 5.11.NGPL, same sponsor HPPL, same auth date 08.07.2019, same 317 km, same 19.20 capacity, target 'March 2024', West Bengal -- but now named 'Kanai - Chhata - Panitar'. Every field (sponsor, authorization date, length, capacity, state) is identical across the two register vintages; only the pipeline's public name and terminus changed, via the confirmed regulatory amendment. GEM's own live sheet already carries this exact successor as P6562 (Kanai Chhata-Panitar Gas Pipeline, Status=construction, LengthKnown=317, Capacity=19.20, ProposalYear=2019, StartYear1=2024, LastUpdated=2025-07-17) -- an exact match to the 2024 PNGRB register row. So P2214 and P6562 are not two different projects; P2214 is the pre-2022-amendment name/config of the identical authorized pipeline that P6562 now tracks live. Keeping P2214 as a separate 'cancelled' 250 km/19.2 MMSCMD project double-counts against the one real 317 km authorization. This also resolves the orchestrator's flagged question about P6562 being a possible predecessor/sibling: it is the direct successor, same PID lineage split across two rows.

concerns.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE is not in doubt -- confirmed via 3 independent origins: (1) India's Comptroller & Auditor General (CAG), Report No. 21 of 2016 'Union Commercial Compliance ... ONGC' (https://cag.gov.in/webroot/uploads/download_audit_report/2016/Union_Commercial_Compliance_Report_21_2016_full_report.pdf -- a 3.5MB PDF; url_verifier returns 200-but-'missing expected' on it, the documented large-PDF false negative, so I downloaded it and ran `pdftotext -layout` locally: 'HUT' is glossed in its abbreviations table as 'Heera Uran Trunk line', and the report describes it by name repeatedly, e.g. 'Crude oil from the offshore platform is despatched to Uran through two pipelines, Mumbai-Uran Trunk line (MUT) and Heera Uran Trunk line (HUT)' and reports a measured 3.09% MUT/HUT metering discrepancy for the Aug-2014-to-Aug-2015 period, i.e. both lines were flowing and being audited in that window); (2) Offshore Magazine, 'ONGC reports Heera-Uran pipeline leak' (2007-12-10, https://www.offshore-mag.com/pipelines/article/16797928/ongc-reports-heera-uran-pipeline-leak, url_verifier OK) -- 'ONGC has reported a leak on the Heera-Uran Gas pipeline in the Heera field ... This will lead to temporary curtailment of about 0.5 MMcf/d of gas to consumers from the Uran processing plant'; (3) the sheet's own cited ISOPE 1991 conference paper 'Design, Construction And Commissioning Of Heera-Uran Trunkline Project' (Jayachandran & Shiv Anand) -- I could not fetch onepetro.org directly (Cloudflare 403 on every route, including the resolved article URL, so it fails url_verifier and is NOT cited here), but its title/authorship/1991 date is independently indexed in a digitized ISOPE-91 proceedings TOC mirrored on yumpu.com (page 335, Vol. II) -- that mirror itself also fails url_verifier (paginated document viewer, no extractable body text), so it is not cited either, but it corroborates the paper is real and dated 1990/91, consistent with the sheet's StartYear1.

CLASSIFICATION is the real problem. GEM's OWN live ResearcherNotes cell on this exact row already says: 'Mainly a crude oil pileine but designed to "transport oil and gas"' -- citing that same onepetro paper -- yet Fuel is still set to 'Gas' and the row carries a gas-only Capacity of 5.84 bcm/y. This is a standing, self-flagged, never-resolved divergence (the standing-rules 'ResearcherNotes documents a deliberate GEM divergence -- verify, don't overwrite' case), and my independent CAG read corroborates the prior researcher's flag rather than resolving it either way: the CAG report treats HUT EXCLUSIVELY as a crude-oil trunk line -- part of ONGC's offshore-to-Uran crude custody-transfer/measurement chain, structurally identical to and paired with MUT (P0944 in this same roster, also gas-tagged, also missing a GOIT twin except MUT's twin DOES exist as P5191) -- with only the 'off-gas' (dissolved gas liberated from the partially-stabilised crude and separated at Uran plant) counted toward gas production after the fact. The 2007 Offshore Magazine leak report, in contrast, calls it a 'Gas pipeline' -- but the scale it describes (a leak curtailing just 0.5 MMcf/d, i.e. roughly 5 mmcm/y) is three orders of magnitude below the sheet's claimed 5.84 bcm/y (~565 MMcf/d) nameplate capacity, which is far more consistent with 'gas' here meaning a small entrained/associated-gas stream riding along a much larger crude pipeline than with HUT being a dedicated 565-MMcf/d gas transmission line. I checked GOIT (data/GOIT_oil_ngl_snapshot_20260810.csv) for a 'Heera' entry that could be the oil-tracker home for this pipe's dominant commodity -- none exists (only P5191 'Mumbai High - Uran Trunk Oil Pipeline' and retired P5192 'Bombay-Uran Trunk Oil Pipeline', both MUT-side, not HUT). So P0926 is not a duplicate of anything in GOIT or in this GGIT roster (checked all 35 rows -- no other pipeline shares HUT's endpoints/spec), it is simply the SOLE GEM record for a pipe that is, by the regulator-grade CAG source and by GEM's own prior note, majority crude oil. Recommend Update decide: reclassify/split, or explicitly document as a deliberate multi-commodity exception with a corrected capacity basis.

concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's StartState/Province for this row is 'Ahal', but every independent source I could find places the pipeline's Turkmenistan starting point in Mary Region, not Ahal. The source gas field, Galkynysh, is itself located in Mary Province (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galkynysh_Gas_Field: 'located in Mary Province... near Yoloten'; offshore-technology.com's own Galkynysh field page independently states the same). The TAPI project page (offshore-technology.com) states the pipeline 'begins from Mary region of Turkmenistan.' I found no source anywhere that supports Ahal as the correct province. This looks like a genuine data-entry error, not a difference-of-opinion or a legitimate alternate framing -- three independent sources (Wikipedia's Galkynysh Gas Field article, offshore-technology.com's Galkynysh Gas Field project page, and offshore-technology.com's separate TAPI project page) all converge on Mary.

concerns.researcher_notes: Nellore (official name since 2008: Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore district) is in Andhra Pradesh, not Tamil Nadu -- and the entire pipeline corridor lies inside Andhra Pradesh. Two mutually-independent PNGRB primary documents confirm this directly: (1) the Aug-2015 bid-application route map shows the KVN pipeline running Kakinada -> Rajahmundry -> Vijayawada -> Guntur -> Ongole -> Nellore, entirely within Andhra Pradesh (with Telangana only appearing as an inset/neighboring-state reference, never crossed by the route), split into a 'Kakinada-Vijayawada Section 170 KM' and a 'Vijayawada-Nellore Section 355 KM'; (2) the PNGRB NGPL MIS register lists 'passing_through_states' / 'States from which pipeline passes' as 'AP' / 'Andhra Pradesh' only, in both the June-2021 edition and the current May-2026 edition. The ONLY source that says Tamil Nadu is the Apr-2018 Indian Infrastructure article -- and it gets this wrong in its own headline AND its own lead sentence ('IMC Limited has received permission from the PNGRB to lay a natural gas pipeline from Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh to Nellore in Tamil Nadu'), even though the SAME article's next sentence names the intermediate towns as 'Rajahmundry, Vijayawada, Guntur and Ongole' -- all unambiguously in Andhra Pradesh, contradicting its own Tamil Nadu claim. GEM's EndState/Province='Tamil Nadu' looks like it was copied from this single erroneous press report rather than any PNGRB primary source. Separately and independently of the Tamil Nadu error, the Start* columns are internally swapped on the sheet: StartPrefecture/District='Andhra' is a truncated STATE name (should be a district), and StartState/Province='East Godavari' is actually the DISTRICT Kakinada is in (East Godavari district, Andhra Pradesh) -- the two values need to trade places and the state name needs to be completed to 'Andhra Pradesh'.

This is a real, government-authorized dedicated (single-customer) pipeline, not a GEM-only entity -- both Length (90 km) and Capacity (6.5 MMSCMD) match the GEM row exactly. Because it is a DEDICATED pipeline (not common-carrier), it correctly does not appear in the PNGRB NGPL MIS register crosswalk (batches/india-gas/staging/register-crosswalk/register_crosswalk.json already classifies P1435 as ABSENT_DEDICATED_OR_TIE_IN, reason 'Torrent PLL-DGEN-Sugen power-plant feeder; dedicated' -- confirms this is expected, not a gap). PipelineType='transmission' is the closest fit in GEM's 3-value vocab (transmission/gathering/distribution) for a long-distance point-to-point industrial gas supply line; there is no 'dedicated/captive feeder' category, so this is a reasonable classification with a caveat noted, not an error. ATTRIBUTION FINDING: GEM's Owner1 is 'Torrent Energy' (100%), but BOTH PNGRB primary documents unambiguously name the applicant/counterparty as 'Torrent Power Limited' / 'M/s Torrent power limited', and the addressee is the Executive Director of 'Torrent Power Limited, SUGEN Mega Power Project'. That Wikipedia article makes no mention of any 'Torrent Energy' entity, and I found no independent evidence anywhere (including a Bing web check) of a company called 'Torrent Energy' active in Indian power/gas. gem.wiki mirrors GEM's own 'Torrent Energy' attribution, so it is not an independent corroboration of the name. Two independent origins (PNGRB regulatory correspondence + Wikipedia/public record) converge on Torrent Power, not Torrent Energy -- recommend the value correction above. concerns.recommendation: Add SegmentCostYear=2018 to date the existing $7bn SegmentCost figure, and flag for re-verification closer to any FID announcement -- do not treat $7bn as a durable current estimate. Consider noting the $10bn figure (the more commonly cited industry-database estimate, e.g. offshore-technology.com's project page) as a documented alternate in ResearcherNotes.
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's SegmentCost of $7,000,000,000 USD traces to a real, specific, dateable statement: in November 2018 TAPI Pipeline Company CEO Muhammetmyrat Amanov told an industry conference in Abu Dhabi that the project's cost had been cut ~30% from an original $10bn estimate to about $7bn (with a first-stage cost of ~$5bn). I verified this exact figure on two outlets -- dawn.com/news/1445485 and business-standard.com/article/reuters/tapi-pipeline-ceo-says-first-gas-to-pakistan-in-around-two-years-118111301159_1.html -- but both are visibly the same Reuters wire story ('UPDATE 1-Tapi gas pipeline to move forward after decades of delays', Reuters, Nov. 13 2018, also cited on gem.wiki itself) republished by two outlets, which per the corroboration rule counts as ONE source, not two independent ones. Separately, cost estimates for this project have varied widely across time and source: $10bn is the figure most commonly given by industry-database pages describing the project in general terms (offshore-technology.com's TAPI page currently states '$10bn'), and other secondary compilations cite figures from $4-5bn up to $7.6bn and $8bn at various points. Given (a) the $7bn figure is a single-wire-origin quote now 7+ years old, (b) it was explicitly framed even at the time as an aspirational cost-cut target tied to a since-repeatedly-slipped FID, and (c) more recent describe-the-project sources default to $10bn, I'm flagging this as a spec concern rather than silently endorsing $7bn as current. I am not proposing to overwrite the value outright since it IS a real, sourceable historical figure -- just recommending it be dated and re-checked.

concerns.recommendation: Correct StartYear1 from 2025 to ~2021 (evidence-backed; exact month uncertain). concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's StartYear1=2025 is contradicted by PNGRB's own multi-year NGPL register history for this exact line (PL Unique ID 5.08.NGPL, entity IOCL, 1,431 km / 84.67 MMSCMD -- unchanged identifiers throughout, so this is unambiguously the same authorisation being tracked over time): as-on 31.03.2021 (captured in NGPL-25062021.pdf), the register already lists 165.82 km OPERATING / 1,265.18 km under construction, with the 165.82 km segment's own target date ('Feb, 2021') already met. That 165.82/1,265.18 split is IDENTICAL across the Sep-2021, Dec-2021, 31.03.2022 ('Partially Commissioned Common Carrier Natural Gas Pipelines' table) and May-2022 editions -- a full year of zero further progress despite a slipping target (Feb 2022 -> June 2022). By 31.12.2022 operating length had grown to 281.80 km; by the Feb/June-2024 editions it had jumped to 1,080 km (75%); by March-2025 to 1,087 km; June-2025 to 1,094 km; and the current May-2026 report shows 1,121 of 1,431 km (78.3%) operating, gas already flowing at 5.9 MMSCMD, with 310 km still under construction and the target completion date ('Mar-25' per the current report) already lapsed. So first commercial gas on this corridor happened by early 2021 at the latest -- roughly four years before the sheet's recorded StartYear1=2025 -- and construction has proceeded in slow, repeatedly-delayed phases since (Trap #3: sectional commissioning, not one event), consistent with the PNGRB register being the origin of Capacity/Length on this row (per country guidance, citing it is correct but not independent corroboration for those two fields) while remaining independent, primary evidence that the recorded START date is wrong. NOTE ON VERIFICATION: url_verifier's automated substring check FAILs on both PDFs cited here because they are large multi-page scans/reports and the extractor does not reach the relevant page (page 5 of 15 in the May-2026 report; page 15-16 of 16 in the 2021 report) -- this is the documented 'large PDF' limitation in url_verifier.py's own header comments. Both URLs return live 200s, and I independently confirmed the exact matching rows via direct PyPDF2 text extraction (page-anchored, quoted in this note), which is the prescribed workaround.

concerns.recommendation: Remove/blank LengthKnown=6900 for P0928 (or footnote heavily) — it is sourced only insofar as it is the printed total for a 13-route regional program, not a corroborated length for a single India-Myanmar-Bangladesh line.
concerns.researcher_notes: Same two sources as the classification finding state explicitly: 'Thirteen routes with a total length of about 6,900 km of pipelines have been proposed for the purpose' (Daily Star, citing The Economic Times) — i.e. 6,900 km is a sum across 13 separate proposed pipelines for NE India's gas/LPG/diesel connectivity plan, most of which are domestic (e.g. the Contai-Haldia-Duttapulia line named in the same article), not one India-Myanmar-Bangladesh route. No source anywhere gives a length for a single cross-border line; Prothom Alo (2026-08-04) explicitly says of the currently-discussed pipeline that 'it remains unclear ... what route the pipeline would take' — i.e. there is still no length to cite for a real single pipeline as of today. Material disagreement between the sheet's implied claim (one pipeline, 6,900 km) and what the sources actually support (a 13-route program totaling 6,900 km) -> spec concern, not silently passed.

concerns.recommendation: Re-examine StartYear1=2025 -- it doesn't match either plausible reading of 'start year' for this phased system. If StartYear1 is meant to record first commercial gas flow anywhere on the line, the true value is 2019 (Phase-1 Phulpur-Dobhi-Barauni section, PM-inaugurated 2019-02-17) or, per the phased-commissioning convention this country already uses elsewhere (Mallavaram-Bhopal-Bhilwara-Vijaipur's P0938/P3602 split), consider whether a separate operating-row split is warranted here too rather than one blended date. If StartYear1 is meant to record the (moving) target full-completion year, the correct current value is 2026, not 2025 -- every source found that discusses a target date (PNGRB register's own 'Dec-25', PSU Watch's 2025-04 'extended to December 2025', and CGDIndia's 2026-03 'revised from March 2026 to September 2026') shows the target has already slipped past 2025 without the line-wide Status ever having been 'operating'. Either reading makes 2025 unsupported by current evidence; flagging to Update rather than guessing which convention applies.
concerns.researcher_notes: Traced the target-completion date across time (classic 'commissioning is sectional, not an event' trap for this country): PSU Watch (2025-04-09, independent trade press) reports GAIL had, as of that date, ALREADY revised the completion timeline for the remaining Durgapur-Haldia and Dhamra-Haldia sections from March 2025 to December 2025, citing Right-of-Use clearance delays, with 97.6% of pipe laid and 96.6% commissioned at that point. PNGRB's own May-2026 NGPL MIS register (the sheet's cited source family) still lists this authorisation's target completion as 'Dec-25' with 257 of 3,546 km still under construction as of that report -- i.e. the Dec-2025 target had already lapsed by the time the May-2026 edition was printed. CGDIndia (2026-03-27, independent of PNGRB) reports the timeline has been revised AGAIN, this time to September 2026. So the documented target-date sequence is roughly March-2025 -> Dec-2025 -> (lapsed) -> Sept-2026, a real, repeated slip -- not evidence the line is now fully operating, and not consistent with the sheet's StartYear1=2025 under either a first-gas or a target-completion reading. Separately, first PARTIAL gas is well dated to 2019-02-17 (PM Modi's inauguration of the 585 km Phulpur-Dobhi-Barauni section with Patna/Varanasi spurlines, contemporaneously reported by millenniumpost.in), six years before the sheet's StartYear1. Status itself ('construction') is NOT in question here -- see status_reviews -- only the StartYear1 value.

concerns.recommendation: Update LengthKnown from 690.00 to 744.00 km (keep LengthKnownUnits=km). The 690 km figure was the 2019 authorization-stage design length; the actual built/authorized-and-supplemented system is materially longer.
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's current LengthKnown=690.00 traces to the 2019 PNGRB authorization's time-schedule table (390 km main trunk + 300 km spur), independently corroborated at the time by the 2019/2021-era forest-clearance note ('approximate length ... 690 kms'). But every source describing the ACTUAL project scope from the 2022 foundation-stone ceremony onward gives a materially larger figure, consistently, across four years and multiple independent origins: GAIL's own 2022-11-12 press release states 745 km (620 km Odisha + 125 km Andhra Pradesh); cgdindia.net's independent coverage of the same 2022 ceremony also states 745 km; cgdindia.net's separate 2025-06-24 construction-progress article (independent reporting, predates the 2026 disclosure) states 744 km as 422 km main + 322 km spur; offshore-technology.com's trade-data profile (GlobalData network, a separate compiler) independently states '744km-long'; and GAIL's own 2026-01-03 stock-exchange disclosure (reprinted by indianmasterminds.com and psuconnect.in) again states 744 km (422+322). Four independent origins across 2022-2026 converge on ~744-745 km, versus one 2019-vintage design-stage estimate at 690 km -- the current sheet value is stale/superseded, not merely uncertain. Tier=high (>=2 independent, non-derivative sources for the 744 km figure alone, without even counting the corroborating 745 km strand).

concerns.recommendation: Re-examine ConstructionYear=2021. No source found supports 2021 as any milestone in this project's history; the best-evidenced construction-start milestone is the PM Modi foundation-stone ceremony on 2022-11-12.
concerns.researcher_notes: The sheet carries ConstructionYear=2021 with no ref (MISSING_REF). I could not find any source -- primary or press -- placing a construction-start event in 2021. The documented timeline is: EOI filed 2017-06; PNGRB authorization granted 2019-07-23 (36-month commissioning clock starts here, targeting ~2022); foundation stone/ground-breaking ceremony 2022-11-12 (PM Modi, per both GAIL's own press release and independent cgdindia.net coverage of the same event); mechanical completion of the 422 km main line by mid-2025 (cgdindia.net, 2025-06-24); commissioning 2025-09-26 and PM dedication 2025-10-16. There is a real gap between the 2019 authorization and the 2022 foundation stone -- three years of front-end engineering/land acquisition is plausible but I found no evidence that pipe-laying itself began in 2021. Flagging as a genuine, sourced discrepancy for Update to resolve (either correct to 2022, per the ceremonial/construction-start convention used elsewhere in this batch, or if 2021 reflects some documented pre-ceremony mobilization Update can locate, keep it and add that ref) rather than silently overwriting.

concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's LengthKnown=667.00 km matches the PNGRB NGPL MIS register exactly in both the archived 25-Jun-2021 edition and the current 31-May-2026 edition (both read '...Kakinada-Vijayawada-Nellore...667...18.0...AP'), so the sheet faithfully carries the regulator's post-authorization register figure -- but that figure conflicts with two documents that predate or are contemporaneous with the actual Feb-2018 authorization. Independently, the Apr-2018 Indian Infrastructure article reporting the actual PNGRB approval states 'The 522 km long pipeline...'. A ~142-145 km (22-27%) gap between the pre-authorization/at-authorization figures (522-525 km, from two independent artifacts) and the post-authorization register figure (667 km, consistent across two register editions five years apart) is large for ordinary route micro-adjustment. concerns.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2023: I could not find a source that states outright 'commissioned in 2023.' What I found instead triangulates loosely around it: the 2016 PNGRB report shows the line only 265/455 km built (41% short); by mid-2024 Indian Infrastructure reports it 'operating at 48 per cent capacity utilisation' (i.e. flowing gas, but well under nameplate); the current (May 2026) PNGRB report shows it 440/455 km 'operating' length under the fully-OPERATIONAL section, no length still tagged 'under construction.' A market database, offshore-technology.com (https://www.offshore-technology.com/marketdata/sultanpur-jhajjhar-hissar-gas-pipeline-india/, url_verifier OK on 'Sultanpur'), describes a '135km-long Sultanpur-Jhajjhar-Hissar' segment 'expected to commence operations in 2022' as part of a 'larger 304km Chainsa-Jhajjhar-Hissar system' -- a rough, one-year-off match to GEM's 2023, but I am NOT proposing it as a ref: (a) it names a different segment ('Sultanpur-Jhajjhar-Hissar', not the pipeline's GEM name), and (b) its '304km' total system length flatly conflicts with PNGRB's 455 km authorised length (confirmed identically in two PNGRB editions ten years apart) -- since this vendor database is already wrong on the one figure I can check against a primary regulator, I don't trust its 2022 completion date enough to stage it either, not even at low tier. Net: StartYear1=2023 is a reasonable estimate of when construction crossed some completion threshold, sits within the plausible window bounded by 2016 (41% built) and 2026 (97% built), but is not independently confirmed to the year -- flagging as an unresolved caveat rather than passing it silently. DIAMETER (a known India-gas gap per the orchestrator's guidance): the same offshore-technology.com page gives 'Maximum Diameter: 12 inches' for the Sultanpur-Jhajjhar-Hissar segment -- the only diameter lead I found for this pipeline -- but for the reasons above (wrong segment name, and the source's own length figure already conflicts with the regulator) I am not confident this 12in applies to the full 455 km trunk GEM records under P0912, so I am leaving Diameter blank rather than staging a number I can't stand behind.

concerns.researcher_notes: PNGRB's own current line-wise register -- the May 2026 'NGPL MIS Report' (https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, page 2, fetched and read locally with pdftotext -layout; url_verifier returns a false-negative HTTP 200/'value not found' on this large PDF per the known limitation, so I confirmed the numbers by hand) lists 'Dabhol-Bangalore' (entity GAIL, authorisation date 14.11.2011) under the PARTIALLY COMMISSIONED COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE section, NOT under Operational: Authorised Length 1,414 km, Authorised/Design Capacity 16.0 MMSCMD (matches GEM's Capacity exactly), Operating Length 1,182 km, Under-Construction Length 232 km, and zero lowered/welded/hydrotested length recorded against that 232 km residual, with a 'Target date of completion' of Feb-13 (i.e. February 2013) that lapsed more than thirteen years before this report -- meaning the regulator's own figures show zero measurable progress on the remaining ~232 km for over a decade, i.e. it reads as stalled/dead rather than actively under construction. This conflicts with GEM's row, which shows a SINGLE fully `operating` segment at LengthKnown=1,386 km (no companion under-construction row exists for P0915 in the wider GGIT gas CSV -- confirmed by grep against the full snapshot). 1,386 km is itself well corroborated -- citizenmatters.in (independent, 2018) states the identical figure ('for about 1,386 km'), so GEM's number is not invented -- but it doesn't equal any of PNGRB's own figures (not the 1,414 km authorised total, not the 1,182 km PNGRB currently calls 'operating'); it sits in between. A plausible explanation surfaced from the sheet's own gem.wiki citation list: Wikipedia (read for leads only, not cited) notes the pipeline's original scope 'also extends to Vasco da Gama, Goa', and one of the wiki page's OWN cited references is a Nov 2010 Outlook India piece titled 'Goa: Farmers Oppose Underground Gas Pipeline' -- i.e. a Goa spur ran into land-acquisition opposition around 2010. That Outlook URL now 410s (confirmed dead, cannot cite per the never-delete-but-can't-cite-a-404/410 rule) so this is not proposed as a citable ref, but it is consistent with PNGRB's residual 232 km being the stalled/abandoned Goa extension while the Maharashtra-Karnataka trunk (the part everyone agrees was completed and dedicated in Dec 2013) is fully operating. Net effect: existence/ownership/classification/start-year/capacity are solid (see prior validity entry); it is specifically the completeness of the authorised corridor -- and therefore whether `Status=operating` should cover 100% of a 1,386 km line or should be split -- that is unresolved.

I could not locate a fourth, tie-breaking numeric source (Wikipedia's HVJ article does not itemize DVPL separately; PNGRB's current monthly register reports only the combined 6-pipe 'Integrated HVJ' system total of 6,169 authorised / 6,732 operating km, not the DVPL-I component alone; a GAIL EOI PDF that a web search summary claimed contained a 'HVJ 1179 / GREP-VDPL 456 / DVPL 610' breakdown was fetched and read directly -- that breakdown does NOT actually appear anywhere in the document, a hallucinated citation I am flagging and discarding rather than repeating). Given the disagreement, I am NOT proposing a replacement value; this needs a human decision on which figure (or which vintage/definition of the route) GEM should carry, so verdict=concern rather than a silent pass. CAPACITY: GEM's Capacity=107.00 MMSCMD/CapacityUnits=MMSCMD is IDENTICAL across all five components of the integrated system in the 35-row roster (P0919, P0925, P3297, P3298, P3299 all = 107.0) -- consistent with the sweep's known India pattern of GEM assigning the combined-system authorised capacity to each split component rather than that component's own individual throughput (DVPL-I's own original design capacity per the GAIL letter was 23.9 MMSCMD in 2004, since grown via later upgrades that are properly attributed to the other component rows). This is explainable/expected per the sweep's scope guidance (do not propose collapsing the rows), so not flagged as a duplicate defect, but it does mean 107.00 does not represent DVPL-I's own capacity and it is now stale versus the current PNGRB reading: the 31-May-2026 monthly register (link above) lists the 'Integrated HVJ' system's current Authorised/Design capacity as 111.3 MMSCMD (natural gas supplied 80.3 MMSCMD, 75.0% utilisation) -- a further ~4% drift beyond the shared-attribution issue. Noting both points for Update; not proposing an edit to Capacity myself since the correct fix (component-level split vs. system total, and which vintage) is a judgment call outside this sweep's scope.

concerns.recommendation: flag for Update: decide whether LengthKnown=1375 should stay as the original trunk-only figure or be updated to the current total-network figure; do not silently keep 1375 without noting which reading it is
concerns.researcher_notes: LENGTH is genuinely ambiguous across sources, and the two readings differ by ~8-10%, which is material. GEM/current sheet: LengthKnown=1375.00 km. Sources supporting ~1375-1400 (an ORIGINAL-TRUNK reading, at commissioning): Wikipedia's own body text states 'EWPL is a...pipeline across the entire trunk length of around 1375 km' (exact match to GEM, though Wikipedia's own infobox on the SAME page instead gives 1,386 km -- the two disagree with each other by 11 km, evidently different vintages of Wikipedia's own editing); Gulf Interstate Engineering's contractor case study (verified) rounds to 'almost 1,400 kilometers'. Sources supporting ~1459-1485 (a CURRENT-TOTAL-NETWORK reading, including spurs/dedicated lines added since commissioning): PNGRB's 31-May-2026 register gives authorised length 1,459 km and operating length 1,485 km for this exact pipeline (row 5, OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER table; confirmed via pdftotext, url_verifier false-negative as documented above); the operator PIL's own corporate site (manually confirmed, not machine-verifiable per the SSL note above) explicitly says 'an overall Pipeline Network of 1485 km, INCLUDING SPUR AND DEDICATED PIPELINE' -- i.e. PIL itself frames 1485 as the full network with branches, distinct from the core 48in trunk. This is consistent with the country-scope guidance's point that PNGRB/operator figures can legitimately exceed an originally-recorded trunk length as a network is built out with spurs over 15+ years of operation (commissioned 2008-2009; PNGRB authorisation itself is dated 21.06.2019, i.e. re-authorised/expanded well after initial commissioning). I am NOT proposing a replacement number since the current GEM value (1375) IS explicitly supported as a valid 'trunk length' reading by Wikipedia's own prose, and correcting to 1485 would be substituting a different SCOPE (total network incl. spurs) for what GEM appears to be recording (the mainline trunk) -- exactly the kind of granularity call the guidance says needs a human decision, not a mechanical overwrite. Flagging as a concern rather than a silent pass so Update makes that call explicitly and, if the total-network reading is preferred, updates LengthKnown with a source note explaining the scope change.

concerns.recommendation: flag for Update: StartYear1=2008 vs the operator's own 'commissioning in 2009' -- confirm which convention GEM intends (construction-complete vs first-gas/commercial-commissioning) before treating 2008 as settled
concerns.researcher_notes: START YEAR disagreement between sources that both look reasonably authoritative. Sources for 2008 (construction completed): Wikipedia's infobox states 'Commissioned 2008' (citing a now-dead gie.com link) and 'Construction started 2006'; independently, Gulf Interstate Engineering's own Wayback-archived case study (verified OK) -- Gulf was RIL's EPCM contractor on this project, i.e. a first-party engineering account, not a tertiary aggregator -- states 'Constructed from 2006 through 2008'. That is two GEM-independent sources agreeing construction finished in 2008, which is what GEM's StartYear1=2008 currently reflects. However, the CURRENT operator's own corporate website (pipelineinfra.com/operations/, read directly, not machine-verifiable per the SSL false-negative noted in the existence finding above) states plainly: 'Since the commissioning in 2009, PIL has been evacuating Natural Gas from upstream facilities of RIL, ONGC and GSPC on the East Coast...' -- i.e. the entity that actually operates the asset today dates its OWN commissioning to 2009, not 2008. A plausible reconciliation (not confirmed, offered as a lead for Update): RIL's KG-D6 field -- this pipeline's original and named gas source (FuelSource=Krishna Godavari Basin) -- began first gas production in April 2009, so construction/mechanical completion in 2008 and first commercial gas flow ('commissioning' in the operational sense PIL's site uses) in 2009 are both plausible and not mutually exclusive; I could not find a single source that states both dates together to confirm this reconciliation explicitly, so I am not proposing a StartYear2 addition without better evidence. Given a live, current first-party statement from the asset's own operator conflicts with GEM's existing value and its (dead-link-sourced) Wikipedia citation, this is a genuine, material disagreement on a date field and should not be silently passed.

concerns.recommendation: correct StartYear1 from 1997 to 1987 (or 1987-88 if a two-value field is available) -- 1997 is the commissioning year of the separately-tracked GREP expansion (P3297), not of HVJ itself
concerns.researcher_notes: SPEC check on StartYear1. GEM carries StartYear1=1997 for P0925/HVJ. This is contradicted by every independent source found, all agreeing on 1987 (some giving 1987-88 to reflect India's April-March fiscal year): (1) GAIL's own 27.11.2018 tariff letter to PNGRB, Annexure-A para 1.1 (OCR-confirmed, see existence finding above): 'was commissioned in 1987-88'; (2) GAIL's own 2021-22 Sustainability Report Glimpses timeline graphic (same PDF as the Length finding, `pdftotext -layout` line ~165-167): 'India's first natural gas pipeline- Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) commissioned' positioned under the year '1987'; (3) Wikipedia's HVJ Gas Pipeline article (verified OK, contains '1987'): 'Construction started in 1986 and the system was commissioned in 1987'; (4) offshore-technology.com's marketdata entry (verified OK, contains '1987'): 'Commissioning Year: 1987'. Four independent origins (two of them GAIL's own primary materials) all say 1987, none says 1997. The likely explanation: 1997 is when the SEPARATE GREP expansion project was commissioned -- per the same GAIL tariff letter para 1.2, 'GREP-- Later, during the year 1997... the HVJ pipeline capacity was expanded... by laying a new 36" x 505 Km pipeline from Vijaipur to Dadri' -- and GREP is already independently tracked in the roster as its own row (P3297, Vijaipur-Dadri Gas Pipeline (GREP-I), updated 2023-07-13). It looks like HVJ's own StartYear1 was set to its expansion's commissioning year rather than its own. This is a genuine, fixable date error, not a judgment call, and warrants verdict=concern rather than a caveat.

concerns.recommendation: flag Capacity=107.00 MMSCMD for Update review as a probable system-total-vs-segment mismatch, consistent with the same pattern already flagged on sibling row P0919 (DVPL-I) in this sweep -- do not silently pass
concerns.researcher_notes: SPEC check on Capacity. GEM's Capacity=107.00 MMSCMD for P0925 (HVJ) is IDENTICAL to the value carried on all four sibling rows in the 35-row roster that make up the same integrated system: P0919 (DVPL-I)=107.0, P3297 (GREP-I)=107.0, P3298 (DVPL-II)=107.0, P3299 (GREP-II)=107.0. This is very unlikely to be five coincidentally-equal, independently-measured segment capacities; it reads as the SYSTEM-WIDE total design capacity copied onto every constituent row rather than each project's own incremental capacity. Two independent primary/regulatory sources corroborate the aggregate interpretation, not a segment-specific one: (1) GAIL's own 2018 tariff letter to PNGRB gives the incremental capacity buildup explicitly -- HVJ alone at commissioning: 18.4 MMSCMD (1987-88); after GREP: 33.4 MMSCMD (1997); after DVPL-I: ~57.3 MMSCMD (2004); after Upgradation Phase-I: ~68.3 MMSCMD (2010); after Upgradation Phase-II/DVPL-II: combined system total ~111.3 MMSCMD (2013) -- HVJ's OWN capacity, by this account, was never 107 MMSCMD at any point; that number only appears once every later expansion project is added in. (2) The current PNGRB monthly register's 'NGPL under Regulation 17' table lists the 'Integrated HVJ' asset (GAIL, authorised length 6,169 km) with Design/Determined Capacity = 107.0 MMSCMD -- an exact match to GEM's value, but explicitly at the SYSTEM level (spanning HVJ+GREP+DVPL-I+DVPL-II/Upgradation combined), not the HVJ segment alone. This is the same finding already independently staged on sibling row P0919 (DVPL-I) in this sweep, which additionally notes the figure is now ~4 points stale versus the current PNGRB main-table authorised/design capacity of 111.3 MMSCMD. I am not proposing a replacement number for P0925 myself -- whether Capacity should be split per segment (18.4 MMSCMD for HVJ's own historical increment) or consistently labeled as the current system total (111.3, refreshed) is a judgment call for Update, and is a cross-row (not P0925-specific) data-convention question. Flagging as concern rather than a silent pass per the sweep's spec rule that a source must AGREE with the GEM number, not merely mention the pipeline -- here the two sources found actually corroborate a different quantity (the system total) than what a literal reading of the column (this segment's own capacity) would imply.

concerns.pipeline_name: High Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid Network
concerns.recommendation: Do not paste GEM's current Length/Capacity refs as-is -- both look stale (~2016-vintage authorisation) against the current PNGRB register. Route to Update: candidate replacement is LengthKnown ~2,860 km authorised (or 2,748 km operating -- GEM's own convention on sister rows P0916/P0917 matches 'authorised', not 'operating', so 2,860 is the more likely fit) and Capacity ~36.0 MMSCMD design/determined (currently-realized capacity, matching the 29.0 MMSCMD/80%-utilisation actually being supplied) rising to an authorised ceiling of 44.8 MMSCMD once the under-construction Anjar-Palanpur expansion is complete. Do not silently overwrite -- this needs a human Update decision on which PNGRB column (authorised vs operating; authorised-capacity vs design/determined-capacity) GEM intends to track.
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's Capacity (31.00 MMSCMD) matches EXACTLY the 'Authorised Capacity' figure printed in PNGRB's Jan-2016 register (31.000 MMSCMD, entry dated 27.07.2012) -- not a coincidence; the same exact-match pattern holds on a sister India gas row researched the same week (P0916 Dadri-Bawana-Nangal: sheet 886.0 km / 31.0 MMSCMD = the 2016 register's figures to the decimal, vs the current register's 921 km authorised / 998 km operating). That means the sheet's Length (2,207.00 km, close to but not exactly the 2016 register's 2,239.0 km -- an unexplained ~32 km/1.4% shortfall even against its own apparent vintage) and Capacity (31.00 MMSCMD) both reflect an authorisation snapshot from roughly a decade ago, not the pipeline as it stands today. The CURRENT PNGRB register (May 2026, row 13, p.2) shows this same network at Authorised Length 2,860 km / Operating Length 2,748 km -- a ~620 km / ~28% network-length increase since the 2016 vintage -- and Authorised Capacity 44.8 MMSCMD / Design-Determined Capacity 36.0 MMSCMD, both well above the sheet's 31.00. This is independently corroborated, not just a PNGRB-internal revision: the March 2025 Business Upturn piece (verified live, distinct origin from PNGRB) reports GSPL's PNGRB-approved capex to raise 'the overall capacity of GSPL's High-Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid to 44.76 MMSCMD' via a new 274 km/30in Anjar-Palanpur line tying into the grid's existing 36in Mundra-Arpar pipeline -- which lines up almost exactly with the register's 44.8 MMSCMD Authorised Capacity line, and explains why 'Design/Determined' (36.0, the currently-realized capacity) is still below 'Authorised' (44.8, the approved ceiling once that expansion is finished, per the article a ~3-year build from its March 2025 approval). This also matches the currently-supplied 29.0 MMSCMD / 80% utilisation figure sitting comfortably under the 36.0 design capacity but nowhere near the sheet's stale 31.00. I am NOT proposing a specific replacement Length/Capacity ref pair myself (per standing rule 3, url_verifier flags both large pngrb.gov.in PDFs as content false-negatives even though I hand-confirmed the numbers with pdftotext, and per the sweep's own India guidance a Length/Capacity disagreement here is very likely a stale-authorisation story rather than a unit error) -- this is a value disagreement for Update to resolve with a human call on which PNGRB column GEM intends to track, not an auto-apply.

concerns.recommendation: Route to a status-review pass: verify whether this dedicated tie-in has ever carried commercial gas volumes and re-derive StartYear1 from an actual first-gas date rather than the terminal's original commissioning announcement; do not treat 2021 as confirmed. Consider adding a ResearcherNotes caveat on the 'operating' status pending that check.
concerns.researcher_notes: STATUS/START-YEAR plausibility concern, not an existence concern - the pipe itself is real and PNGRB-confirmed mechanically complete (see the spec entry above). The problem is that this is a DEDICATED single-purpose tie-in whose only intended gas source is the Jaigarh LNG import terminal, and that terminal's own history makes GEM's StartYear1=2021 look wrong and the unqualified 'operating' status worth re-checking: (1) the terminal's FSRU (its only regas unit, Hoegh Giant) did not even arrive at Jaigarh until 1 March 2022 - a year AFTER the terminal's originally-announced 'March 2021' commissioning target (nsenergybusiness.com project page) - so no LNG could plausibly have reached this pipeline as early as 2021; (2) Hoegh LNG terminated the FSRU charter in April 2022 over 'the charterer's default of the contractual terms' and withdrew the vessel from India entirely (two independent LNG Prime articles, both verified live); (3) I found no report of a permanent replacement FSRU having entered service since; (4) ownership of the whole Jaigarh terminal project changed hands from H-Energy to AG&P Pratham around December 2024 (constructionworld.in, verified live), and as recently as the AG&P negotiation coverage (offshore-technology.com, verified live) the terminal is still described as a stake being acquired/negotiated, not as an operating asset. So for essentially the entire period since this pipe reached its full 60km (PNGRB shows that by mid-2024), its sole supply source has had no working FSRU. GEM's StartYear1=2021 reads like the terminal's originally-ANNOUNCED target year carried over onto the pipeline, rather than an actual first-gas date - a recognized failure mode (dating an asset from an announcement instead of an outcome). I could not independently confirm actual gas throughput either way (PNGRB's tie-in table does not publish the gas-supplied/capacity-utilisation columns that its main common-carrier tables do), so I'm flagging rather than proposing a specific corrected value - Delayed=yes/DelayType=confirmed IS well supported by this same evidence and needs no change.

concerns.recommendation: No sheet change. Flagging so a future researcher who finds the original 2010 PNGRB order does not mistake its provisional figures (834.81 km / 4.0 MMSCMD common-carrier capacity) for an error in the current sheet values (877.86 km / 16.00 MMSCMD).
concerns.researcher_notes: I pulled and OCR'd the actual primary source cited on gem.wiki for this row's Start/Length/Capacity citations -- PNGRB's original authorization letter, No.Infra/PL/Exis/17/KG-REG/GAIL/01/10 dated 12 May 2010 (a scanned/image PDF with no extractable text layer; pdftotext returns 0 lines, so I ran pdftoppm + tesseract on all 4 pages). That letter states verbatim: 'the said pipeline project which has already been completed and commissioned between year 1991 to 2005' -- this directly and explicitly supports StartYear1=1991 as the start of that range; it is a primary regulatory finding of fact (based on GAIL's submitted proof), not a guess or an authorisation-date mix-up. HOWEVER the same 2010 letter also states: 'The capacity of K.G. Basin Natural Gas Pipeline network, length 834.81 kms, diameter ranging from 2 inches to 18 inches, is equal to 15.997 MMSCMD as indicated by GAIL... The common carrier capacity would thus be 4.0 MMSCMD*' (footnoted as provisional, pending final capacity determination). So at the moment of authorisation (2010) the network was 834.81 km / ~16 MMSCMD total capacity but only 4.0 MMSCMD DECLARED COMMON-CARRIER capacity. Every later PNGRB register edition I could check -- Jan 2016 ('877.9 km, 16.000 MMSCMD'), Feb 2024 ('877.86 km, 16.00 MMSCMD authorised, 19.4 MMSCMD design/determined, 864.90 km operating'), and May 2026 ('878 km authorised, 16.0 MMSCMD authorised / 19.4 MMSCMD design, 867 km operating') -- instead shows an AUTHORISED CAPACITY of ~16 MMSCMD (matching GAIL's originally-indicated total network capacity, not the 4.0 MMSCMD provisional common-carrier figure) and a LENGTH that grew from 834.81 km to 877.86-878 km sometime between 2010 and Jan 2016. I could not locate the specific intermediate order that finalised the higher capacity determination or authorised the extra ~43 km (candidate mechanisms: the 2010 letter's own final-capacity-determination clause, or subsequent GAIL applications not captured in these three summary tables), so I am not proposing a value change -- GEM's current 877.86 km / 16.00 MMSCMD is the value used consistently by the regulator for the last decade (2016-2026), while the 2010 figures are a superseded historical baseline. Treating this as a caveat, not a live disagreement, per the instruction to note material history rather than silently pass it.

concerns.recommendation: Correct StartYear1 to 2013 (August 2013). 2019 is the commissioning year of a different, later-built stretch of the same overall KKBM project (the ~440-444 km Kochi-Mangalore leg), not this 44 km Phase I segment.
concerns.researcher_notes: Sheet: segment 'Phase I', LengthKnown=44.00 km, StartYear1=2019. Cross-checked against the sheet's own cited leads (wiki_citations.json) plus one open-web source. NS Energy Business project database (independent industry pipeline-project profile, cited by the wiki page itself) states explicitly: 'The Kochi-Koottanad-Bangalore-Mangalore pipeline project was split into two development phases with phase one involving a 41km-long pipeline section between Kochi and Koottanad in Kerala... The phase one section of the pipeline was successfully completed and commissioned in August 2013.' Indian Express (2021-01-11, also cited on the wiki page) independently corroborates the length: 'In the first phase, a 44-km line was laid in Kochi, linking the terminal with local industrial users, including Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited.' Both sources describe the SAME 41-44 km first-phase segment (rounding difference only) and both place it years before 2019 (approved June 2009, commissioned Aug 2013). The 2019 date instead matches NS Energy's description of Phase II's Kochi-Mangalore sub-segment ('the 440km pipeline stretch between Kochi and Mangalore via Koottanad which was successfully completed and commissioned in June 2019') -- a different, much longer stretch that is NOT captured by this 44 km row. So the sheet has paired the correct Phase-I length with the wrong phase's commissioning year. Two independent sources agree on both the 44 km figure (confirming LengthKnown) and on 2013 as Phase I's actual completion year (contradicting StartYear1=2019) -> high tier on the length confirmation, high tier on the date correction.

concerns.recommendation: correct StartYear1 from 2021 to 2019 (commissioned 14 October 2019 per GITL's own regulatory/credit disclosures) -- 2021 appears to conflate the pipeline's own commissioning with RFCL's (the sole offtaker's) unrelated urea-plant COD in March 2021
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's StartYear1=2021 does not match either independent source I could find. CARE Ratings' two press releases (13-Sep-2023 and 08-Dec-2025, both confirmed via pdftotext, verifier false-negative documented above) state unambiguously: 'GITL commissioned phase-I of the MBBVPL on October 14, 2019.' The wiki's own cited source (PNGRB's 'Partially Commissioned Common Carrier Natural Gas Pipelines', 31 March 2021 edition) only documents that the pipeline WAS ALREADY commissioned as of that March-2021 snapshot -- it is a status-as-of date, not a commissioning date, and 2021 is also exactly when CARE separately notes 'RFCL commissioned its urea project in March 2021' (a different asset -- the customer's fertiliser plant, not GITL's pipeline). The most likely explanation is that GEM's StartYear1 was set from the March-2021 PNGRB snapshot (or from RFCL's own March-2021 COD) rather than from GITL's actual commissioning date, which is a full 17 months earlier. I could not find a second, organizationally distinct source giving the specific Oct-2019 date (CARE's two reports share one analyst house, so I'm treating them as one origin for tier purposes), so tier=medium rather than high, though I'm confident in the direction of the correction given CARE repeats the identical date across two independently-commissioned annual credit reviews three years apart, each presumably re-verified against GITL's own filings.

concerns.recommendation: flag/verify Capacity=78.25 MMSCMD for this 'Phase I' row -- independent sourcing indicates the ACTUAL design capacity of the 365 km built/operating Phase I stretch is only ~4.5-5 MMSCMD (of which ~2.02 MMSCMD is contracted to RFCL); 78.25 (rounds to PNGRB's 78.3) is the AUTHORISED/system-wide design capacity for the FULL 1,881 km project once entirely built (Phase I + the still-under-construction 1,517 km Phase II), not the capacity of the segment this row actually describes
concerns.researcher_notes: This is the most material finding on the row. GEM's Capacity=78.25 MMSCMD for the 'Phase I' segment matches PNGRB's regulator table almost exactly (78.3 MMSCMD, 1dp rounding) -- but that PNGRB figure is explicitly the 'Authorised/Design Capacity' for the ENTIRE GITL entity/project (Authorised Length column = 1,881 km, i.e. the whole corridor, not the 365 km operating stretch). Two independently-sourced, organizationally distinct citations establish the actual built Phase-I capacity is far smaller: (a) CARE Ratings, in both its 2023 and 2025 press releases (same house, but each an independently re-verified annual credit review): 'The design capacity of phase-I is ~4.50 mmscmd [2025]/around 5 mmscmd [2023], of which ~2.02 mmscmd is supplied to RFCL under a GTA'. (b) Business Standard, a mainstream Indian business daily, reporting contemporaneously in July 2016 on the signing of the actual RFCL Gas Transportation Agreement (https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/gitl-signs-transportation-agreement-with-ramagundam-fertilizers-for-20-years-116071500658_1.html, verified OK): 'Under the agreement, GITL will supply 2 mmscmd of natural gas from Mallavaram of Andhra Pradesh to RFCL's plant at Ramagundam' -- an independent, decade-old, pre-CARE confirmation that the actual contracted/designed throughput for this exact stretch is single-digit MMSCMD, not 78. The mechanism is also independently explained: CARE's disclosures (and a related PNGRB/GITL diameter dispute, corroborated in a November-2019 APTEL appellate tribunal judgment I located via indiankanoon.org/aptel.gov.in but could NOT cite -- both mirrors failed url_verifier, one on a gov.in SSL certificate-chain error and one on a 403, so I am not proposing them as refs, only reporting what I read) state GITL built the 364.42 km Phase-I stretch at 18-inch diameter instead of the originally-contracted 42-inch, specifically 'leading to reduced capacity with respect to the authorised capacity' -- i.e. the smaller pipe physically cannot carry anywhere near the 78 MMSCMD full-system design figure. I am NOT proposing a replacement Capacity value myself (per the no-forced-numbers guidance and because 4.5 vs ~5 vs the CARE 2.02-contracted figure are three different granularities of the same underlying fact) -- this is a genuine value disagreement for Update to resolve, most likely by changing Capacity to ~4.5-5 MMSCMD for this Phase-I-scoped row (or by adding a ResearcherNotes caveat if GEM deliberately intends this field to describe the ultimate system capacity rather than this segment's actual capacity). tier=high: CARE and Business Standard are two organizationally independent origins, seven years apart, agreeing on the same order-of-magnitude, non-78 figure.

concerns.recommendation: Route to Update for a joint P0941/P5411 review, not a mechanical refresh: (1) LengthKnown=1,177 km and Capacity=80.11 MMSCMD were accurate for GEM's July-2023 vintage but are now stale -- PNGRB's current (31 May 2026) edition shows operating length 1,339 km and authorised/design capacity 83.1 MMSCMD for this asset; (2) before applying that refresh, reconcile it against CARE Ratings' August-2024 COD declaration (1,417.80 km completed, 276.2 km permanently de-scoped from the financed project) and the June-2025 update (three spur lines still under active construction, one 130 km Bhatinda-Jalandhar trunk stalled on RoW) -- PNGRB's 'under construction' 604 km bucket and CARE's 'de-scoped' framing describe overlapping but not identical things and need a human read before either P0941's operating length or P5411's construction length/status is edited; (3) verify StartYear1=2022 -- CARE's own filings put Phase-I-in-GIGL's-own-numbering (442 km) as operational since November 2018, four years earlier, and GEM's 'Phase I' (1,177 km) does not map 1:1 onto GIGL's company phase-I/II/III scheme, so 2022 may reflect a later commissioning milestone rather than first gas; confirm which milestone GEM intends before changing it.
concerns.researcher_notes: LENGTH/CAPACITY: cross-checked GEM's LengthKnown=1177.00/Capacity=80.11 MMSCMD against a sequence of PNGRB's own monthly/periodic NGPL registers, fetched independently via Wayback Machine archives of pngrb.gov.in's own PDFs (none GEM- or wiki-authored): 31.03.2022 edition (op. length 1,030 km / UC 910 km / capacity 80.11 MMSCMD -- https://web.archive.org/web/20231225124427/https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/NGPL-23052022.pdf), a Dec-2022 edition (op. 1,153 km / UC 787 km / capacity 80.11 -- https://web.archive.org/web/20240628103021/https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/NGPL-02122022.pdf), and a 21.02.2024 edition (op. 1,200 km / UC 740 km / capacity 80.11 -- https://web.archive.org/web/20241121235526/https://www.pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/NGPL-21022024.pdf). GEM's recorded value of 1,177 km sits exactly between the Dec-2022 (1,153) and Feb-2024 (1,200) readings, and the LastUpdated date (2023-07-20) matches the wiki's own citation retrieval date for PNGRB (cite_note-:3-4, 'Retrieved 2023-07-20') -- so the sheet value was correct for its vintage, corroborated by two independent regulator snapshots bracketing it in time, not a research error. However it is now materially stale: the CURRENT PNGRB edition (31 May 2026, cited above) shows operating length 1,339 km (+162 km / +13.8% vs GEM) and authorised+design capacity 83.1 MMSCMD (+2.99 / +3.6% vs GEM) -- this remains an actively-commissioning 'partially commissioned' asset (target completion date in the current PNGRB edition has slipped to Jun-2026). STATUS COMPLEXITY (why this is not a simple refresh): CARE Ratings' 30-Aug-2024 press release (cited above) states the ENTIRE financed project achieved commercial operations date (COD) on 22 August 2024 for 1,417.80 km, with the remaining 276.2 km of originally-scoped construction 'de-scoped' (removed from the debt-financed project and its associated debt surrendered, ₹5,076cr sanctioned reduced to ₹4,289cr). The June-2025 update (cited above) clarifies this did NOT mean abandonment: GIGL is still actively building three spur lines (NFL Bhatinda, HPCL Mittal Energy, Jodhpur connectivity -- expected complete FY26/FY27, funded separately outside the original project debt) while a 130 km Bhatinda-Jalandhar trunk section has 'no movement... due to RoW issues.' This means PNGRB's current 604 km 'under construction' figure and CARE's 276.2 km 'de-scoped' figure describe an overlapping but not identical picture (differently-funded, differently-timed pieces of the same residual scope), and it is not safe for me to mechanically translate either into a length/status edit on P0941 or its paired construction row P5411 -- that judgment call belongs to Update. STARTYEAR: GEM records StartYear1=2022 for this 'Phase I' (1,177 km) row. CARE Ratings (both vintages, independently) states 'phase-I, including 442 kms of natural gas pipeline, achieved commercial operations date (COD) in November 2018' -- but GIGL's own phase-I/II/III numbering (442 / ~944 / ~308 km per CARE) does not correspond to GEM's two-row operating/under-construction split (1,177 / 763 km), so I cannot conclude GEM's 'Phase I' StartYear should simply become 2018; it may legitimately represent a later cumulative-commissioning milestone. status_changes.researcher_notes: This is not a dormancy inference (no silent >=2y/4y clock) -- it is a confirmed regulatory event. Three independent outlets (boldnewsonline 2023-02-22; psuwatch and business-standard, both 2023-06-22) report that PNGRB formally cancelled/foreclosed GIGL's original 2011 Bhatinda-Jammu-Srinagar authorization at Gurdaspur after GIGL missed its build deadline, and disqualified GIGL/GSPL from re-bidding the Gurdaspur-onward stretch, which GAIL then won in June 2023 (now GEM's P5413, under construction). GIGL's Bhatinda-Gurdaspur portion (P3913) was unaffected and remains its own live authorization -- so 'cancelled' applies to the ROW AS RECORDED (the single 725 km GIGL-owned entity), not to the underlying physical corridor, which is very much alive under successor authorizations GEM already tracks separately. The still-open remainder -- a new ~325 km Jammu-Srinagar tender PNGRB invited bids for in Jan-2024 (deadline 2024-05-13) -- has produced no award, construction-start, or cancellation news I could find through Aug-2026 (18+ months of apparent silence since the bid deadline), but that is a distinct, not-yet-tracked entity and doesn't bear on what Status P0908 itself should carry. Recommend Update also consider whether that open tender warrants a fresh Discovery row rather than folding it back into a revived P0908.

This is an affirmative regulatory-cancellation finding, not a dormancy inference, so the 2y/4y staleness rules do not apply. PNGRB's own Annual Report 2019-20 (p.46, section 3.8 'Cancellation of authorisations') states in its own words: 'Ennore-Nellore Natural Gas Pipeline: Authorization issued on 2nd December, 2014 ... in favour of Gas Transmission India Private Limited (GTIL) had to be cancelled by the Board on 30th October, 2019, under the provision of the extant regulations, as GTIL failed to achieve FC and Capacity booking/Natural Gas Tie-up and there has been virtually no progress in the execution of the pipeline project ... The Performance Bank Guarantee of Rs.7.3 Crore was accordingly encashed by the Board. Subsequently, the order of the Board for cancellation of the authorisation has been challenged by GTIL before the APTEL.' Consistent with this, the same report's own 30-June-2020 'Natural Gas Pipelines under construction' table (Annexure listing) does NOT include Ennore-Nellore at all -- it had already dropped off PNGRB's own live-authorization list within a year of cancellation. The later APTEL judgment (26 April 2024, Appeal Nos. 331/332/361 of 2022 & 13/636/640 of 2023, an unrelated CGD-bidding case that references ENPL only as background) states as settled fact: 'the authorization of ENPL pipeline was cancelled by PNGRB vide order dated 20th December, 2022 which was upheld by this Tribunal vide its judgement dated 4th October, 2023' -- and repeats this a second time later in the same judgment ('ENPL ... cancelled by the Respondent-Board on 20th December, 2022'). Reading the two PNGRB-family documents together, the most coherent procedural picture is: Board cancels (30 Oct 2019) -> GTIL appeals to APTEL -> a further/confirming Board order issues (20 Dec 2022), possibly after remand or renewed default -> APTEL upholds cancellation (4 Oct 2023) -> referenced again as settled in the April 2024 judgment. I could not independently pin down whether the Dec-2022 date is a second cancellation order or the AR2019-20's report of the *original* 30-Oct-2019 date is simply superseded terminology in the later document -- flagging this dating nuance for Update to resolve if precision matters, but it does not affect the bottom-line verdict: BOTH the regulator and its own appellate tribunal treat this authorization as formally and finally dead, well past mere shelving. I set CancelledYear=2019 (the initiating Board order) rather than 2023 (final appellate confirmation) since 2019 is when the Board's cancellation action actually occurred; recommend Update confirm which year GEM's convention prefers (initiating order vs. final-on-appeal) before applying. PNGRB's live May-2026 MIS register (https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf) still lists the line under 'under construction' with the original 2014/Apr-2020 dates -- this is administrative non-removal of a cancelled authorization (the register apparently isn't purged of formally-cancelled lines, distinct from Trap #4's 'never retires an unsurrendered authorisation' pattern, since here PNGRB itself already acted to cancel it) and should NOT be read as evidence the project is alive. Both PDF url_verifier checks FAIL via the automated script (SSL cert-chain error on aptel.gov.in; large-PDF extraction miss on the multi-hundred-page AR2019-20) but both are documented false-negative patterns in url_verifier.py's own docstring; manually confirmed live (curl 200) and content-matched (pdftotext -layout / pypdf extraction quoted verbatim above).

This matches the exact Trap-#4 pattern the country guidance describes for P0921 Ennore-Nellore: a live PNGRB authorization sitting in the 'under construction' section with 0 km built and a lapsed target is good evidence FOR shelved/dormant, not evidence of active construction. Here the case is arguably stronger than a single lapsed target: PNGRB's own register shows the completion target has ALREADY slipped once (Feb-2021 in the June-2021 edition -> Mar-2024 in the current May-2026 edition) and even the revised Mar-2024 target is now more than two years overdue as of the report date. Every single progress metric in the current register row reads zero: operating_length_km=0, hydrotested_length_km=0, lowered_length_km=0, welded_length_km=0, out of 667 km authorised -- i.e. not partial progress, but literally no recorded physical construction activity across at least the five years spanned by the two register editions I could compare (2021, 2026), despite an authorization now over 8 years old (19-Feb-2018). Unlike P0921, I found no formal PNGRB cancellation order for this line (nothing like the AR2019-20 cancellation-notice language) -- this is a dormancy inference from the register's own progress columns and slipped target, not a documented cancellation, hence 'shelved'+ShelvedCancelledType='inferred' rather than 'cancelled'+'confirmed'. I did not fabricate a ShelvedYear -- the exact point at which the project went dormant (vs. merely slow) isn't pinned down by the evidence I have; leave that field for Update to set only if a firmer basis turns up. CAVEAT: my session's web-search budget was exhausted before I could run a fresh open-web search for any 2023-2026 trade-press coverage of this specific pipeline (construction updates, IMC statements, financial-closure news) that might independently corroborate or contradict the register's zero-progress picture -- the PNGRB register itself is the only evidence base for this call, and while it is the single most authoritative source available for exactly this question (it IS the regulator's own physical-progress audit), it is one institution, not corroborated by a second independent origin the way the P0921 cancellation was. Flagging tier=medium/independent=false for that reason; recommend a follow-up open-web pass on 'IMC Kakinada Vijayawada Nellore pipeline' before this status change is applied.

The newest dated evidence I could find is the gem.wiki page's own citation #2, a PNGRB 'Under Construction Dedicated Natural Gas Pipelines' list dated 31 Mar 2021 (retrieved by GEM 2021-09-03) -- i.e. still under construction as of March 2021. This is a cross-border India-Nepal MOU-stage proposal, so PNGRB's register (which covers only the Indian domestic common-carrier grid) does not carry it and cannot be used, per the country guidance. Newest independent evidence I could find naming this specific corridor is the Kathmandu Post's 2023-04-30 report of an April-2023 Nepal-India JWG meeting, where it is STILL described as 'another proposed gas pipeline' with no progress beyond the words 'to study feasibility' first used in Jan 2020 -- three-plus years and at least four JWG meetings (2018, Jan-2020, Aug-2020, Apr-2023) produced zero forward movement on this specific line. I checked for anything more recent: the most recent Nepal-India JWG meeting I could find coverage of is the 5th meeting (scheduled Dec 8, 2025, per Asian Lite / Omm Com News / The Hindu, all dated 2025-12-03) -- its reported agenda covers ATF/aviation-fuel pipeline supply via the Lothar extension, LPG pipeline/storage, and the Siliguri-Jhapa products pipeline, with NO mention of the Gorakhpur-Rupandehi/Bhairahawa gas line. A separate March-2026 Nepal proposal for a gas pipeline (Khabarhub, 2026-03-24) is a different, unrelated corridor (Motihari-Sarlahi), not this one. So as of today (2026-08) there is no independent evidence this project has been discussed at all since April 2023 (3.3 years), and it has been implicitly dropped from the active JWG agenda in favor of other India-Nepal pipeline projects (ATF, LPG, products). Applying the dormancy rule for a 'proposed' project with no progress for >=2 years: recommend Status -> shelved, ShelvedCancelledType=inferred, no fabricated ref per standing rule 2. This is an inference from absence of evidence, not a sourced status-change announcement, so proposed_refs is intentionally empty.
