No explicit cancellation/withdrawal notice was found anywhere on PNGRB's site -- this is an INFERRED dormancy call, not a confirmed one, and closes one of the 8 blank-ShelvedCancelledType gaps flagged for this cluster. Timeline: GAIL filed the EOI 17.11.2020; PNGRB opened public consultation 23.11.2020, closing 23.12.2020, with an open-house session held 04.01.2021 (all per the Public Notice PDF). PNGRB's own EOI registry page shows NO follow-on activity for this Notice No. (PNGRB/Auth/2-NGPL(17)/2020) beyond that -- the page's Comment/MAP/BID link slots for this row are empty/disabled, unlike several other rows on the same page that do carry populated comment PDFs or bid links. I checked all ~20 archived PNGRB NG bid-round listing pages (ng-bid-1.html through ng-bid-20.html): zero mentions of Kondalapalli/Kondapalli/Tirupati, meaning it never converted to either a negotiated authorization or a competitive bid. As of the most current PNGRB register available (NGPL MIS Report, 31-May-2026 edition -- the live authorized-pipeline list), no Kondalapalli/Kondapalli-Tirupati line appears among operating or under-construction authorizations. IMPORTANT CAVEAT per the country brief's warning: absence from the register alone proves nothing (it only lists live authorizations, and this project never got one in the first place) -- what actually supports dormancy here is the combination of (a) zero follow-through on PNGRB's own EOI-tracking page over 5+ years, and (b) zero appearance in any bid round. That is dated evidence of abandonment at the EOI stage, not merely an absence. Given >4 years with no progress past the initial public-consultation step (Dec 2020/Jan 2021 to present, 2026-05), the dormancy rule's shelved->cancelled threshold (4y) is comfortably met, supporting the ALREADY-RECORDED Status=cancelled -- no status change needed, only the vocabulary gap: ShelvedCancelledType should be 'inferred' (not 'confirmed', since no source states an explicit withdrawal, and definitely not 'Presumed', which is not valid vocabulary) and CancelledYear is left unset rather than guessed, since no discrete cancellation date exists to pair with it -- only a stall window (Dec 2020-Jan 2021) is documented, not a formal cancellation event.

Status=cancelled remains correct, so this is not a status flip -- but the supporting metadata is wrong and this is a genuine confirmed-vs-inferred correction, not a dormancy call. Business Standard (dateline Jan 25 2013) reports the government's formal cancellation order for RGTIL's four pipeline authorizations, Kakinada-Haldia included, 'had been issued earlier this month' (i.e. January 2013); RGTIL's own stated reason was falling KG-D6/eastern-offshore output making the line uneconomic. Hindu BusinessLine (published June 5 2012, verified via the page's article:published_time metadata) independently corroborates the immediately preceding stage: PNGRB pushing the Ministry for cancellation over a missed bank-guarantee deadline, with the underlying construction deadlines (36 months from EoI notification / 24 months from full Right-of-User) expiring 'between June and August' of that year. This is a CONFIRMED cancellation (a named government order, independently reported), not our own dormancy inference -- so ShelvedCancelledType should read 'confirmed', matching the sourced event, not 'inferred'. It should also carry CancelledYear=2013 (the year of the actual order), not the sheet's current 2011, which matches no milestone in the documented timeline (authorization 2007-08 -> deadlines lapsing mid-2012 -> PNGRB push June 2012 -> formal cancellation Jan 2013). I found no source addressing the sheet's separate ShelvedYear=2009 and am not proposing a change to it absent evidence either way.

This is the same dormancy signature the country note already treats as grounds for a shelved (not construction) status on P0921 Ennore-Nellore -- a live PNGRB authorisation sitting against a long-lapsed target with zero physical build progress -- and P3602 matches it closely, arguably more strongly given a dedicated primary document. Evidence, oldest to newest: (1) PNGRB Board letter dated 21.06.2019 (Ref Infra/PL/Monitoring/MBBVPL/05, scanned image PDF -- url_verifier FAILs because it has no extractable text layer; manually confirmed by rendering all 3 pages to PNG at 150dpi and reading them directly) states plainly 'GITL has not laid the [balance] pipeline in accordance with the authorization granted to them' as of mid-2019, grants only a further extension to March 2020 conditional on GITL achieving (a) physical laying of a minimum 20% of the balance pipeline length and (b) receipt of 50% line pipe plus EPC contract award for the entire MBBVPL, and states in paragraph 3 that failure to meet these by March 2020 would trigger penalty/termination proceedings against either the entire authorisation or the balance pipeline. (2) PNGRB Annual Report 2019-20 (p.109-111, Sr.No.6; url_verifier FAILs on this large PDF -- a documented false-negative pattern for PNGRB PDFs in this country, manually confirmed via pdftotext -layout) independently repeats the SAME March-2020 target and the SAME ~364 km commissioned figure, and its Annexure F confirms PNGRB held progress-review hearings with GITL on this exact pipeline as late as 10/22/23 September 2020 -- i.e. the March-2020 deadline came and went with the regulator still actively reviewing rather than closing the file. (3) The live 31-May-2026 NGPL MIS register (url_verifier FAILs -- documented large-PDF false-negative, manually confirmed via pdftotext -layout) STILL lists Sr.No.3 with the identical March-2020 target unchanged 6+ years later, operating length still static at 365 km, and -- critically -- welded_length_km=0, hydrotested_length_km=0 and lowered_length_km=0 for the entire 1,517 km 'under construction' balance, i.e. zero physically-verifiable pipe-laying progress reported on any axis the register tracks, for a project whose own regulator was already threatening termination for lack of progress back in 2019. By contrast, genuinely active India under-construction lines in the same May-2026 register report substantial nonzero welded/hydrotested/lowered figures (e.g. Kochi-Koottanad-Bangalore-Mangalore 278/58/275 km, Ennore-Tuticorin 1283/1161/1280 km). All three documents are PNGRB-origin (not mutually independent as an origin, hence tier=medium/independent=false per this country's own convention that PNGRB alone caps at medium), but they span 2019-2026 and are internally consistent, which is why I am proposing a change rather than merely 'confirm'. IMPORTANT CAVEAT / follow-up recommended: this is exactly the situation that, on the sibling case P0921 Ennore-Nellore, turned out on deeper research to be a FORMAL CANCELLATION (PNGRB Board order 30.10.2019, upheld by APTEL) rather than mere dormancy -- the register there also still listed the cancelled line unchanged for years, which is the identical presentation I am seeing here. This is the trap-4 pattern this country's guidance specifically flags (Ennore-Nellore/P0921 precedent): a live PNGRB authorisation sitting in the 'under construction' register bucket is NOT itself evidence of activity, and a lapsed target with zero physical progress is evidence FOR shelved/dormant, not for construction. Checked the actual line item (not the section aggregate) across THREE dated editions: 2025-06-30, 2025-10-31 (both pdfplumber-confirmed directly by me: 'Kanai - Chhata - Panitar HPPL 08.07.2019 317 19.2 ... 0 317 0 0 0 Mar-24 WB' -- operating length 0, hydrotested 0, welded 0, lowered 0, under-construction-remaining 317 of 317, target Mar-24), and the repo's independently reconciled 2026-05-31 extraction (batches/india-gas/staging/register-crosswalk/pngrb_ngpl_mis.json, verified against the report's own printed totals), which shows the identical zero-progress reading. Three consecutive editions spanning at least eleven months (Jun-2025 -> Oct-2025 -> May-2026) show NO movement whatsoever on any physical-progress metric, against a target completion (Mar-2024) that is now more than two years overdue. Independent (non-PNGRB) context: the Hooghly District Magistrate's land-acquisition notices for this exact project are dated Feb-Apr 2024 -- i.e. land acquisition was still underway right around the original target date, consistent with the project having been far from completion when it was supposed to finish, and I found no notices or news newer than Apr-2024 indicating the acquisition process (let alone actual pipe-laying) progressed further. I found no independent news story explicitly declaring the project shelved, cancelled, or abandoned -- only the absence of any progress signal since. This is a 'stale' verdict under the dormancy rules, treated the same way this country's guidance treats a stalled 'under construction' register entry with a lapsed target and no physical progress (staleness_rule '2y->shelved' is the closest of the two given rules -- I'm applying the 2-year-no-progress logic to a 'construction' status that has produced literally 0 km of welded/hydrotested/lowered pipe for at least the eleven months I could directly measure, and against a target that lapsed over two years ago). NOT recommending 'cancelled' -- the authorisation is still live and PNGRB has not delisted it, which only supports 'shelved', not 'cancelled'. The existing sheet ref for Status (pngrb.gov.in/eng-web/data-bank.html#bm6 / #bm7) itself fails url_verifier's content check for 'construction' (it passes for Fuel/PipelineType) -- it is a generic/dynamic portal anchor, not a citable line item; recommend replacing it with the MIS report PDF citations above regardless of which way the Status question resolves. Flagging this for human review rather than unilaterally downgrading -- Baird should weigh in given PNGRB itself still lists it as 'under construction' on paper.
